title: overlay: fall back to diff dir size when XFS quota lookup fails
body:
ReadWriteDiskUsage only consulted the XFS quota controller and returned its error directly. When the quota lookup fails, fall back to sizing the "diff" directory, and only surface an error when the fallback also fails, joining both errors so the original quota failure is preserved.

I noticed the discrepancy between the comment and the code by reading it, I didn't run into this issue in a live environment.

comments.body:
OTOH, uh… `ReadWriteDiskUsage` has no `store`-level API (and no user in Podman), the only way to reach it is to via `store.GraphDriver()` — as CRI-O does.

But that also means it is completely bypassing the c/storage locking :/

CRI-O only calls ReadWriteDiskUsage on writable container layers, so the only failure that could really happen is from the quotactl syscall: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/storage/drivers/quota/projectquota_supported.go#L331-L337

But as you hinted, the scenarios in which the syscall would fail are very limited in production and in the main cases would mean that an administrator deliberately modified the container writable layer, which is very unlikely.

>  in such a way that falling back to a very costly method is desirable?

Although it is very costly, the walk is the common method used by all the other graph drivers. The fallback would bring reliability by making the overlay driver consistent with the other.

Based on all of this, I think falling back is a bit overkill and unnecessary.
If you think the same, I can update the PR to reflect in that in the comment.

I mean… you know why you filed this PR. Did you hit this in production? If not, is there some other reason you are concerned about this code?

---

> Based on all of this, I think falling back is a bit overkill and unnecessary. If you think the same, I can update the PR to reflect in that in the comment.

I’m not sure what the proposal is. If it is unnecessary, the code should not exist, so the comment would say “we did not do this unnecessary thing”?

I might not have been clear enough, but as I mentioned in the PR description, I didn't run into this in a live environment. I noticed that the comment of the function mentioned a fallback that was not there: https://github.com/podman-container-tools/container-libs/blob/main/storage/drivers/overlay/overlay_disk_quota.go#L11-L13, so I thought it was unintentionally left out.
